description: bfloat16 pair multiply, two lanes per accepted beat (latency 1, not stateful): lane0 is a[15:0]*b[15:0] and lane1 is a[31:16]*b[31:16], each bf16 being {sign, 8-bit exponent (bias 127), 7-bit fraction}. Both lanes decode to the unified form v=mant*2^(Eff-134) with Eff=max(E,1), so subnormal inputs (mant=M, Eff=1) share the normal path, and each lane forms its 8x8 mantissa product with the um8 shift-add recode (eight conditional partial-product adds; operands never exceed 255, so the 16-bit accumulator is exact and no Verilog `*` is emitted). The exponent fields are added and the product's leading-one position picks a single round-to-nearest-even step: result exponent field = Ex+Ey+p-141 with the mantissa shifted right p-7, and when that field would be <= 0 the lane instead takes the subnormal grid shift 135-Ex-Ey with the same RNE step, so a rounded-up code of 2^7 correctly becomes the smallest normal. A fraction carry beyond bit 7 increments the field, and a field of 255 becomes a correctly signed infinity. Infinity times a zero (or a NaN) is refused rather than silently turned into a quiet NaN, and any other infinity operand produces the sign-XOR infinity. result[15:0]=lane0 bf16 pattern, result[31:16]=lane1. aux[0]=lane0 infinity, aux[1]=lane0 zero result, aux[2]=lane0 inexact, aux[3]=lane0 rounding incremented, aux[4]=lane0 subnormal-grid path, aux[5..9]=the same five flags for lane1, aux[15:10]=0, aux[31:16]=lane0's 16-bit mantissa product. fault=1 when either lane sees a NaN operand or a 0*infinity pair (result=aux=0).
hardware_advantage: Two independent bf16 products retire per enabled beat on two wired shift-add arrays: each lane is one 8x8 recode plus a wired exponent add and one round-to-nearest-even step, so a pair of ML activations costs one beat, while the same pair through a soft path needs two unpack-multiply-repack subroutines with a normalise branch each.
